checks.note: isolated Site, both Sites. The six new product cases: a product saves with its three names, the deployed default base unit, the batch flag, minimum stock and default cost, and two unit rows with their factors and default marker; the roster and detail read back; switching the default leave exactly one; two defaults, a repeated unit name (with padding) and a unit without a factor are each refused with no product stored; an exact factor (0.1) and price survive the round trip; deactivation hides it, include_inactive lists it and deleting clears the child rows; permissions cover a read-only role and a product of another company; all nine RPCs refuse anonymous callers (403).

checks.command: docker exec ... python -m unittest test_cowork_product_units test_cowork_client_records test_cowork_buyer_resolve
checks.note: the master-data family's pure modules still pass; this batch changed none of them

intentional_differences: the units are a child table of the product rather than a separate table, so they cannot exist without their product; the deployed product_active synchronisation on each unit row is not ported because the problem it addressed (a lookup that hides products of disabled parents) does not arise here

an update that carries units replaces the whole child table instead of patching row by row; the row-level rules (including an explicit None clearing a nullable column) stay in the ported pure module for when row editing is needed
the product has both a display name and the three-language name triple, while the deployed row used one name column; the presentation rule still reads the triple, as deployed

two unit rows asking to be the default are refused rather than silently reduced to one, and a repeated unit name is checked case-insensitively before writing because a child table carries no unique constraint
not_run: the buyer import normalisation, supplier and tax-profile master data, settings and categories, real product data, the frontend, deployment and user acceptance
